text:
alex (support): Customer report: several 429s plus spikes in p50/p95 latency starting ~18:20 UTC. They say it started after a small feature rollout. Sample error from customer: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` with headers: 
  X-RateLimit-Limit: 6000
  X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
  X-RateLimit-Reset: 1672

maya (eng-sre): Can you paste the tenant_id and a request_id from one 429? We can correlate in the limits dashboard.
alex (support): tenant: tenant_8f3b, req: r_20260317_4521. Customer says requests are small (single-turn chat) but bursty: many simultaneous calls.
maya (eng-sre): OK pulling logs now. Quick hint: look at per-route token breakdown and the per-tenant sliding-window. If they're doing many concurrent short requests, continuous batching may not help and the quota meter will show sudden bucket depletion.
ratebot: Alert: tenant_8f3b exceeded burst_quota window at 2026-03-17T18:19:58Z (429s emitted).
jamal (billing): Also seeing an invoice anomaly flagged — high token count yesterday. Might be related if retries are aggressive. Any retry loops on client side?
alex (support): Customer says they retried on 429 with exponential backoff, but backoffs are only 200ms initial. They have 40 clients fanout.
sara (product): If they do immediate retries across clients, that makes the burst worse. Suggest recommending jittered backoff and retry-after honoring.
maya (eng-sre): Repro steps I ran in staging: `ab -n 200 -c 40 -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" '/v1/chat'` -> reproduced 429 tail when per-tenant burst window was hit. Logs show token consumption spike per-route: `model=text-2-large` accounted for 85% tokens.
maya (eng-sre): Dashboard tips: filter by tenant_id -> inspect "burst_window_used" and "sliding_quota_remaining". Check route-level p95 to see fallback routing kicks in. Also check the quota-eviction events for cache pressure.
alex (support): Customer asked for a short-term mitigation while they fix clients. Options?
maya (eng-sre): 1) Temporarily increase tenant burst allowance (can do a one-off override) 2) Enable routing to a cheaper model variant with lower token cost for that tenant 3) Ask them to implement >1s initial backoff + jitter.
jamal (billing): If we raise burst allowance, note it will affect billing. I'll pre-authorize a temporary increase for 24h if they accept.
sara (product): Also propose adding a per-route alert that notifies when sliding quota dips below 10% for any tenant so we catch these before 429 storms.
maya (eng-sre): I'll create a dashboard tile and an alert: query `sum(sliding_quota_remaining) by (tenant)` < 0.1 * quota. Will set a 5m window to avoid noise.
alex (support): Sent customer a triage note with repro steps and temporary options. They asked for an export of the affected request traces. maya, can you attach the traces for r_20260317_4521?
maya (eng-sre): Attached trace link: https://console.redwood/investigations/trace/r_20260317_4521. Payload shows many 1-token messages, high concurrency.
jamal (billing): Customer accepted the 24h burst bump. I'll update billing and record the temporary credit.
sara (product): Follow-up: add docs blurb about retriable 429 handling + client best practices. Could reduce similar tickets.
alex (support): Nice. I'll close this support ticket after customer confirms stability in 12h. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
